schema_note: Reg Deadline Wall data. Every entry carries a source_url and verified_on stamp. date=null means the regime recurs without a single independently-confirmed next-occurrence date this session — recurrence text describes the rule instead. Never edit date/recurrence fields without a fresh primary-source check.

entries.regime: Pillar Two GloBE Information Return (GIR)
entries.jurisdiction: OECD / Global (model rule; local implementation varies by country)
entries.recurrence: 15 months after reporting fiscal year end (18 months for the first / transition year a group is in scope). Date shown is the example first GIR deadline for a calendar-year MNE group's FY2024 transition year.
entries.who_files: Ultimate Parent Entity or designated Filing Entity of in-scope MNE groups (GloBE Model Rules Art. 8.1.6 / Art. 9.4.1)

entries.regime: DORA Register of Information (RoI)
entries.recurrence: Annually, by 30 April, national competent authorities submit the consolidated Register of Information to the ESAs (EBA/EIOPA/ESMA), per the ESAs' standing joint decision on reporting timelines. Entities file to their NCA on an earlier, nationally-set deadline (commonly end of Q1). Date shown is computed from the confirmed recurring 30 April rule, not independently re-confirmed as a 2026-specific published date.
entries.who_files: In-scope EU financial entities under DORA (banks, insurers, investment firms, payment institutions, etc.) via their national competent authority

entries.regime: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation (23 NYCRR 500) Certification
entries.recurrence: Annually, by April 15, for the prior calendar year (23 NYCRR 500.17(b))
entries.who_files: Covered Entities under 23 NYCRR Part 500 (including limited-exemption filers), via the DFS Portal

entries.regime: FFIEC Call Report (031/041/051)
entries.recurrence: Quarterly, due no later than 30 calendar days after the quarter-end report date (35 days for banks with more than one foreign office, excluding shell branches/IBFs). Date shown is the confirmed Q2 2026 (June 30, 2026 report date) standard deadline; the foreign-office extension for the same quarter is August 4, 2026.
entries.who_files: All FDIC-insured depository institutions filing FFIEC 031/041/051

entries.regime: FR 2052a Complex Institution Liquidity Monitoring Report
entries.recurrence: Daily for G-SIBs, Category II firms, and Category III firms with average weighted short-term wholesale funding of $75B or more; monthly for smaller Category III firms and all Category IV firms. Exact intraday submission timing (commonly cited as T+2, 3:00pm ET) was not independently reconfirmed against primary instructions text this session and is omitted.
entries.who_files: BHCs, IHCs, and FBOs subject to Category I-IV enhanced prudential standards (Reg YY/Reg LL) above the reporting threshold

entries.regime: FR Y-14A Capital Assessments and Stress Testing (Annual)
entries.recurrence: Annual, as of December 31. The exact submission-lag deadline (commonly cited elsewhere as early April) was not independently confirmed against primary instructions text this session and is omitted.
entries.who_files: BHCs, IHCs of FBOs, and covered SLHCs with $100B or more in total consolidated assets

entries.regime: FR Y-14Q Capital Assessments and Stress Testing (Quarterly)
entries.recurrence: Quarterly, as of the last calendar day of each quarter (Trading/Counterparty schedules follow a different as-of convention). The exact submission-lag deadline was not independently confirmed against primary instructions text this session and is omitted.
entries.who_files: Same $100B+ panel as FR Y-14A

entries.regime: FR Y-9C Consolidated Financial Statements for Holding Companies
entries.recurrence: Quarterly, due 40 calendar days after the March 31, June 30, and September 30 report dates, and 45 calendar days after the December 31 report date. Filed by top-tier BHCs, SLHCs, IHCs, and SHCs with total consolidated assets of $3 billion or more. Date shown is the Q2 2026 (June 30, 2026 report date) deadline.
entries.who_files: Top-tier bank/thrift/intermediate/savings-and-loan holding companies with total consolidated assets of $3B or more

entries.regime: GENIUS Act — Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuer Monthly Reserve Composition Report
entries.recurrence: Monthly: each permitted payment stablecoin issuer must publish on its own website the composition of reserves backing outstanding stablecoins (total outstanding stablecoins, reserve amount/composition by category, average tenor and custody location for each category), and that same month-end report must be examined by a registered public accounting firm (GENIUS Act, Pub. L. 119-27, section 4). FDIC-supervised issuers additionally file weekly/quarterly regulatory reports under FDIC NPR 2026-04-10. No fixed calendar publication day is set by statute or the NPR, so no single next-occurrence date is shown.
entries.who_files: Permitted payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act

entries.regime: Computer-Security Incident Notification (36-Hour Banking Agency Rule)
entries.recurrence: Event-triggered, not calendar-based: a banking organization must notify its primary federal regulator (OCC 12 CFR Part 53; Federal Reserve 12 CFR Part 225, Subpart N; FDIC 12 CFR Part 304, Subpart C) as soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after determining that a notification incident has occurred. Bank service providers must notify the affected banking organization(s) as soon as possible. Effective April 1, 2022; full compliance required by May 1, 2022.
entries.who_files: Banking organizations supervised by the OCC, Federal Reserve, or FDIC, and their bank service providers

entries.regime: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation (23 NYCRR 500) Incident Notification
entries.recurrence: Event-triggered: a Covered Entity must notify NYDFS as promptly as possible but in no event later than 72 hours after determining that a Cybersecurity Incident has occurred at the entity, an affiliate, or a third-party service provider (23 NYCRR 500.17(a)). Distinct from the entity's annual April 15 certification of compliance (separate entry, same regulation).
entries.who_files: Covered Entities under 23 NYCRR Part 500

entries.regime: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 Material Cybersecurity Incident Disclosure
entries.recurrence: Event-triggered: a registrant must disclose a cybersecurity incident determined to be material within 4 business days of the materiality determination (the clock runs from the determination, not from discovery or occurrence). Adopted July 26, 2023; in effect for most registrants since December 18, 2023.
entries.who_files: SEC reporting companies (domestic registrants filing Form 8-K)

entries.regime: CTC e-invoicing — Belgium mandatory B2B (Peppol)
entries.recurrence: One-time mandate go-live; already in force. Administrative-fine tolerance period ran through end of March 2026 (the obligation itself was not delayed). B2G e-invoicing (orders over EUR 3,000 ex-VAT) has been mandatory since March 1, 2024.
entries.who_files: All Belgian VAT-registered businesses, B2B domestic transactions

entries.regime: CTC e-invoicing (KSeF) — Poland, large taxpayers
entries.recurrence: One-time mandate go-live for taxpayers whose 2025 sales exceeded PLN 200M
entries.who_files: VAT taxpayers with 2025 sales over PLN 200M

entries.regime: CTC e-invoicing (KSeF) — Poland, other businesses
entries.recurrence: One-time mandate go-live for VAT taxpayers not in the large-taxpayer or smallest-taxpayer bands
entries.who_files: VAT taxpayers below the PLN 200M threshold

entries.regime: CTC e-invoicing (KSeF) — Poland, smallest taxpayers
entries.recurrence: One-time mandate go-live, deferred band for the smallest taxpayers
entries.who_files: Smallest VAT taxpayers (deferred band)

entries.regime: CTC e-invoicing/e-reporting — France, receipt (all) + issuance (large/ETI)
entries.recurrence: One-time mandate go-live. All French companies must be able to receive e-invoices from this date; large enterprises and mid-size (ETI) companies must also issue e-invoices from this date. This is the post-delay date superseding the original 2024-2026 schedule.
entries.who_files: All companies (receipt); large enterprises and ETI (issuance)

entries.regime: CTC e-invoicing/e-reporting — France, issuance (SME/micro)
entries.recurrence: One-time mandate go-live for SME and micro-enterprise issuance obligation
entries.who_files: SMEs and micro-enterprises (issuance)

entries.regime: Fedwire Funds Service — ISO 20022 structured postal address requirement
entries.recurrence: One-time compliance date. The fully-unstructured postal address option is removed; participants must use fully structured or hybrid address format with Town Name and Country always present.
entries.who_files: All Fedwire Funds Service participants

entries.regime: Regulation CC funds-availability dollar threshold inflation adjustment
entries.recurrence: Adjusted every 5 years by the change in CPI-W (this cycle measured July 2018-July 2023, a 21.8% increase). Effective date shown is the most recent reset, already in force. Next reset is due around 2030; the exact date has not been announced by a primary source and is not shown.
entries.who_files: Banks and credit unions subject to Reg CC funds-availability schedules

entries.regime: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) Article 50 — Transparency Obligations
entries.recurrence: One-time compliance date, not tied to fiscal periods. Coverage note: Art.50(2) AI-generated-content marking and Art.50(4) deepfake/synthetic-content disclosure are live-covered by the wired 3-node chain ai-content-disclosure-conformance (art-126-ai-act-art50-marking-checker, art-127-dual-layer-disclosure-verifier, art-128-content-binding-assertion-validator; all confirmed status=live in chaingraph.json). Art.50(1) (disclose-you're-talking-to-an-AI-system, e.g. chatbots) and Art.50(3) (emotion-recognition/biometric-categorization operation disclosure) are NOT covered by any live tool or chain — this is a genuine, separately-obligated gap, not a subset of the marking chain. Distinct from Annex III high-risk-system obligations, which apply from a later, separate date (2 December 2027) not shown in this entry. A pending EU Digital Omnibus proposal would delay the Art.50(2) marking sub-duty specifically to 2 December 2026 for systems already on-market before 2 Aug 2026; that proposal was not yet adopted law as of verified_on and is noted, not relied on.
entries.who_files: AI system providers/deployers within Art.50 scope (synthetic-content and deepfake generators for 50(2)/(4); chatbot providers and emotion-recognition/biometric-categorization deployers for 50(1)/(3))

entries.regime: SEC US Treasury Central Clearing Rule — Cash Secondary-Market Transactions (FICC members)
entries.recurrence: One-time compliance date for cash UST transactions (repo/reverse-repo transactions carry a separate, later compliance date of 30 June 2027, not shown in this entry to avoid conflation). Extended 12 months by SEC order dated 2025-02-25 from the original 2026 schedule. Coverage note: 9 live, wired chaingraph.json chains cover this mandate end-to-end — treasury-clearing-fit, treasury-clearing-access-model, treasury-clearing-cross-margin, treasury-clearing-repo-margin, treasury-clearing-collateral, treasury-clearing-capital-relief, treasury-clearing-liquidity, treasury-clearing-onboarding, treasury-clearing-settlement-integrity, plus the umbrella us-treasury-clearing chain (all confirmed present by chain name in chaingraph.json). 8 of the 9 have at least one kernel-backed (art-/sim-/cry-/qfa-/ml- prefixed) step and execute compute; treasury-clearing-collateral's steps are all bare-numeric repo/tools catalog entries with no kernel step, so that one chain is reference/catalog-only and does not itself produce a computed artifact.
entries.who_files: FICC members and their counterparties in eligible cash secondary-market US Treasury transactions

entries.regime: SEC US Treasury Central Clearing Rule — Repo/Reverse Repo Secondary-Market Transactions (FICC members)
entries.recurrence: One-time compliance date for Treasury repo/reverse repo secondary-market transactions (cash secondary-market transactions carry an earlier compliance date of 31 December 2026, tracked separately as sec-ust-clearing-cash). Extended 12 months by SEC final rule dated 2025-02-25 from the original 30 June 2026 schedule.
entries.who_files: FICC members and their counterparties in eligible repo/reverse-repo secondary-market US Treasury transactions

entries.regime: SEC Rule 10c-1a / FINRA SLATE (Rule 6500 Series) Covered Securities Loan Reporting
entries.recurrence: One-time compliance date for covered-party reporting of covered securities loans to FINRA's SLATE facility (public dissemination is a separate, later date — see finra-slate-10c1a-dissemination). Originally extended to 2026-09-28 by SEC order 34-103560 (dated 2025-07-28); that order was itself superseded — following the Fifth Circuit's remand (No. 23-60626) — by SEC order 34-104303 (dated 2025-12-03), which set this later date.
entries.who_files: Covered persons (broker-dealers, banks, and other lenders of reportable securities) under SEA Rule 10c-1a via FINRA Rule 6500 Series

entries.regime: SEC Rule 10c-1a / FINRA SLATE Public Dissemination
entries.recurrence: One-time compliance date for FINRA's public dissemination of aggregated covered-securities-loan data (reporting itself begins earlier — see finra-slate-10c1a-reporting). Originally extended to 2027-03-29 by SEC order 34-103560 (dated 2025-07-28); that order was itself superseded — following the Fifth Circuit's remand (No. 23-60626) — by SEC order 34-104303 (dated 2025-12-03), which set this later date.
entries.who_files: FINRA (as the registered national securities association operating SLATE); consumed by all market participants

entries.regime: Swift CBPR+ MT101 (FI-to-FI) Coexistence End
entries.recurrence: One-time cutover: MT101 payment-initiation messages sent over FIN must migrate to pain.001v9 (MX) via FINplus. After this date, MT101 (multiple) is NAKed and MT101 (single) falls to contingency processing. Distinct from the Fedwire/CHIPS structured-address requirement dated 2026-11-16 (fedwire-iso20022-structured-address) — different network, different obligation, coincidentally two days apart.
entries.who_files: Financial institutions sending/receiving MT101 payment-initiation messages over the Swift network

entries.regime: EU Instant Payments Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/886) — Verification of Payee, non-euro-area PSPs
entries.recurrence: One-time compliance date, extended for payment service providers outside the euro area. Euro-area PSPs have been bound by the same Verification of Payee obligation since 2025-10-09 (already in force, not a future date).
entries.who_files: Payment service providers in non-euro-area EU member states offering credit transfers

entries.regime: DTCC Corporate Actions ISO 20022 Legacy Format Decommission
entries.recurrence: Operator-set milestone schedule (DTCC Important Notice 23890-26), not a regulator mandate: PSE testing began 2026-01, Test Facility opened 2026-03, production testing 2026-07, and legacy (non-ISO-20022) corporate-actions message formats are scheduled for decommission in Q3 2027. No single day-level date is published for the Q3 2027 decommission, so no next-occurrence date is shown.
entries.who_files: DTC participants receiving/processing corporate-actions messaging

entries.regime: CSDR REFIT (Regulation (EU) 2023/2845) — 2026 Provision Dates
entries.recurrence: UNVERIFIED — secondary-sourced only. CSDR REFIT entered into force 2024-01-16 with provisions applying on a staggered schedule; secondary sources (e.g. Norton Rose Fulbright) cite a 2026-01-17 settlement-discipline provision date and a ~2026-12 allocation/confirmation harmonization date, but this session did not independently confirm either specific date against the Official Journal text itself. No date is asserted here pending that primary-source check.
entries.who_files: EU CSDs and their settlement-instructing participants

entries.regime: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by the 2026 Digital Omnibus) — General Enforcement Application
entries.recurrence: One-time application date, NOW IN FORCE (past). From 2 Aug 2026 the AI Office and member-state competent authorities hold enforcement powers; GPAI duties (in force since Aug 2025) now carry enforcement exposure (fines up to EUR 15M / 3% global turnover) and Art.50 transparency duties are enforceable (tracked separately as eu-ai-act-art50-transparency). High-risk application dates were DEFERRED by the Digital Omnibus (in force 2026-07-27): Annex III stand-alone systems to 2027-12-02 and Annex I embedded systems to 2028-08-02, tracked as their own entries.
entries.who_files: Providers and deployers of in-scope AI systems on the EU market; GPAI model providers

entries.regime: EU AI Act — High-Risk Obligations, Annex III (stand-alone) AI Systems
entries.recurrence: One-time application date, deferred from 2026-08-02 by the 2026 Digital Omnibus (European Parliament backed the postponement 2026-03; Omnibus in force 2026-07-27). Classification, risk-management, data-governance, technical-documentation and conformity-assessment duties for Annex III stand-alone high-risk systems apply from this date.
entries.who_files: Providers (and deployers where duties attach) of Annex III stand-alone high-risk AI systems on the EU market

entries.regime: EU AI Act — High-Risk Obligations, Annex I (AI embedded in regulated products)
entries.recurrence: One-time application date for high-risk AI embedded in Annex I regulated products (machinery, toys, medical devices, etc.), deferred from 2027-08-02 by the 2026 Digital Omnibus. Trails the Annex III date by 8 months, mirroring the original Act's embedded/stand-alone stagger.
entries.who_files: Providers of AI systems embedded in Annex I regulated products subject to third-party conformity assessment

entries.regime: EU AI Act (as amended by the 2026 Digital Omnibus) — Prohibition: AI generating/depicting CSAM and non-consensual intimate imagery
entries.recurrence: One-time application date for the Omnibus-added prohibition on AI systems that generate or depict child sexual abuse material and non-consensual intimate imagery (including 'deepfake' depictions of real persons). Prohibitions are hard bans, not compliance duties — no transition, no grandfathering.
entries.who_files: Any provider or deployer of AI capable of generating such material on the EU market

entries.regime: GENIUS Act (US federal payment-stablecoin statute) — Statutory Effective Date
entries.recurrence: Statutory effective date: the earlier of 18 months after enactment (enacted 2025-07-18, so 2027-01-18) or 120 days after final regulations are issued. Most substantive duties (reserve composition, monthly reporting, CEO/CFO certification, prohibited yield) apply from this date. Implementation is in flight: OCC interim rules (Feb 2026: 1:1 reserves, monthly composition + CEO/CFO certification, $5M capital floor), FDIC licensing (Dec 2025) and prudential rules (Apr 2026), FinCEN/OFAC AML (Apr 2026); Treasury issuance/offer-sale NPRM published 2026-08-18 (comments tracked separately as genius-treasury-nprm-comments); Fed, NCUA-substantive and reciprocity rules still open.
entries.who_files: Payment-stablecoin issuers (US and foreign with US market access), qualified custodians, and downstream payment processors

entries.regime: GENIUS Act — Treasury/FinCEN NPRM on Payment Stablecoin Issuance, Offer, and Sale (comment window close)
entries.recurrence: One-time comment-window close, 62 days after publication (Federal Register doc 2026-16796, published 2026-08-18, comments_close_on 2026-10-19 confirmed via the Federal Register API at verification time). Covers §3 issuance/offer-sale definitions.
entries.who_files: Commenters: issuers, banking associations, market participants and the public; final-rule scope follows

entries.regime: Federal PQC Migration (EO + OMB M-26-15) — High-Value Assets: key establishment
entries.recurrence: One-time migration deadline set by OMB M-26-15 (2026-06-24, executing the June 2026 executive order): high-value assets migrate key-establishment algorithms to post-quantum (FIPS 203 ML-KEM family; CNSA 2.0 specifies ML-KEM-1024) by end of 2030. CNSA 2.0 makes PQ signing/networking algorithms exclusive from 2030.
entries.who_files: US federal civilian agencies owning HVAs and high-impact systems

entries.regime: Federal PQC Migration (EO + OMB M-26-15) — Digital signatures
entries.recurrence: One-time migration deadline: digital-signature algorithms migrate to post-quantum (FIPS 204 ML-DSA family; CNSA 2.0 specifies ML-DSA-87 and EXCLUDES SLH-DSA) by end of 2031, one year after key establishment.
entries.who_files: US federal civilian agencies

entries.regime: Federal PQC Migration (EO + OMB M-26-15) — Full civilian-agency migration complete
entries.recurrence: Year-level deadline (the memo says 'by 2035'; 2035-12-31 shown as the year boundary): all federal civilian systems complete post-quantum migration. FIPS 203/204/205 (Aug 2024) are the governing standards; Falcon/HQC standardisation is ongoing and may extend the approved set.
entries.who_files: US federal civilian agencies

entries.regime: Federal PQC Migration (EO + OMB M-26-15) — Agency PQC Migration Plans due to OMB/ONCD
entries.recurrence: One-time submission deadline, 120 days after M-26-15 (2026-06-24 + 120 days = 2026-10-22). Plans must carry a cryptographic inventory (CBOM), risk-based prioritisation of HVAs and internet-facing systems, and crypto-agility as an architectural principle. This is the nearest-term PQC date.
entries.who_files: US federal civilian agencies (PQC migration leads appointed within 30 days of the memo)
